title: GCAL: Adapting Graph Models to Evolving Domain Shifts
summary: Major: the core continuous-feature lower bound is false, and the pinned active memory graph generator has categorical rather than independent-Bernoulli support. Gaussian formula error remains Minor because code uses the correct law. Historical empirical effects unresolved.

problems.title: False information-bottleneck lower bound for continuous memory features

claim.location: Theorem 3.1 PDF p. 4 Eq. (5); Appendix A PDF p. 13 Eq. (21) and PDF p. 14 nonnegativity justification/Eq. (22)
claim.text: J >= E log Pf - beta E KL(Pg(M|G,Z)||Q) + beta E log Pg(M|G,Z); conditional entropy omitted as nonnegative.

assumptions: beta=1; fixed graph with one hundred nodes and one-node real-feature memory
Q exact marginal N(0,.0001); Y constant 0; valid binary classifier Pf(0|M)=.5
All relevant entropies/KLs/MI finite; generated M depends on Z
problems.check: Closed-form Gaussian entropies and mutual informations. Also standard normal-prior pointwise Gaussian Markov-chain example.
problems.result: Primary J=0 and maximized J=0, claimed lower bound 2.4930844722234733. Standardnormal prior example J=-4.258621596333139, RHS=-2.112085713764618.
counterevidence: Discrete finite entropies would permit the drop, but model explicitly has continuous Gaussian features.
MI chain rule and KL bound Eq. (20) are valid.
No benchmark reproduction or empirical-score damage inferred.
Primary construction handles outer max notation; secondary concerns pointwise practical surrogate.

impact.core_dependency: Abstract, contribution 2, Sections 3.2.3-3.2.5 use this bound to motivate generator losses, especially positive conditional log density/LGen term.
impact.boundary: Invalid theoretical foundation supports Major without requiring score loss or failure of entire heuristic.

correction.text: For discrete Y,beta>=0 and finite/ac terms, J>=E log Pf-beta E KL(Pg(M|G,Z)||Q). Removing last term or retaining beta h(M|G) changes objective and does not restore original three-term claim or certify practical repair.

problems.core_dependency: Theorem 3.1 motivates the generator losses, especially the positive conditional log-density term.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: finite continuous-Gaussian counterexamples violate the stated lower bound; discrete entropy nonnegativity does not apply.

acceptance_check.scope: Looser inequality valid under stated finite/absolute-continuity assumptions; original three-term bound not restored.

problems.title: Gaussian reparameterization uses variance instead of standard deviation

claim.location: PDF p. 4 Eq. (7) and explicit log standard deviation sentence

problems.result: Printed sampling identity false; correct multiplier is sigma.
counterevidence: Released VGAE.reparameter uses exp(.5logvar), consistent with correct law.
problems.severity_rationale: Minor: sigma squared as noise multiplier gives the wrong variance; the pinned implementation uses the correct exp(logvar/2).

acceptance_check.scope: Correct printed identity; no historical feature-sampling failure inferred.

problems.title: Pinned edge generator samples row categories instead of independent Bernoulli edges

claim.location: PDF p. 4 Section 3.2.2; GCAL.py PGE.forward lines 30-68; active call path GCAL.py148-167 and253-269
claim.text: Paper independent Bernoulli edges; release row gumbel-softmax then > .8 threshold.

assumptions: PyTorch 2.2.1 default dim=-1 verified in primary source
problems.check: A row summing 1 has at most one entry>.8; two independent Bernoulli(.5) edges coexist with probability .25.
problems.result: Release distribution differs from stated independent edge model.
counterevidence: A later binary-sampling block exists but is unreachable after return.
Acquired commit not established as historical experiment commit.

impact.affected: Core memory graph generation and replay distributions in the pinned implementation
impact.not_established: No proof historical tables used this branch; no measured score effect.
impact.core_dependency: PGE.forward is called by VGAE.decoder at GCAL.py148-152 and replay165-167; generated adjacency enters losses253-269; Bernoulli regularizer157-158.

correction.text: Use independent binary relaxation per edge with correct probability/logit convention, then validate; not implemented.

problems.core_dependency: Active PGE calls feed synthetic memory generation, replay and losses; its regularizer assumes Bernoulli edges.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: row-categorical normalization and threshold impose at most one edge per row, excluding graphs allowed by the core independent-Bernoulli model.
